newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caymans court sentences Canadian fraudster.
newsitem.headline: Caymans court sentences Canadian fraudster.

text.p: A Cayman Islands court sentenced a Canadian man to 15 months in prison on Monday for attempting to pass bogus checks worth about US$682,000.
Denis Rene Desjardins, 57, pleaded guilty to fraud charges.

He told the court he owed C$230,000 (US$166,000) in his hometown, Toronto, and was facing bankruptcy when he came to the islands in May. He tried to set up an offshore company using as an opening deposit checks totalling C$943,485 ($682,000) which he had stolen from his Ontario employer.
Desjardins worked for AdminSource of Toronto, a company which administers mutual funds. He said he stole 200 checks from various accounts that had already been signed by a machine.
He told the court he had C$200,000 ($144,400) in a retirement account but lost it in failed investments. He then had to borrow a further $230,000 which he still owes back in Canada.
He said he had never been in trouble with the law before but he stole the checks as a way out if his problems.
Magistrate Grace Donalds sentenced him to 15 months jail.
The case highlighted the growing problem of white-collar crime involving foreign nationals in this offshore tax haven and financial centre.
